1. Install two packages `gganimate` and `gifski` then restart Rstudio. Using the `Adult Census Income` data, make an animation using `geom_point` and `transition_states`.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gganimate)
library(gifski)
df <- read_csv("https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/adult_census.csv")
df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = hours.per.week)) +
  geom_point() +
  transition_states(marital.status) +
  labs(
    x = "Age",
    y = "Hours Per Week",
    title = "Marital Status: {closest_state}"
  )
```


2. Using the `Adult Census Income` data, make an animation using `geom_bar` and `transition_states`.
```{r}
library(readr)
df <- read_csv("https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/adult_census.csv")


library(gganimate)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = sex)) +
  geom_bar() +
  transition_states(marital.status) +
  labs(
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Marital Status: {closest_state}"
  )
```


3. Use the WHO's dataset at [this link](../data/WHO-COVID-19-global-data.csv). Make a top-10 bar race by months between countries on the number of deaths by Covid 19 in 2021.
```{r}
library(readr)
df1 <- read_csv('https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/WHO-COVID-19-global-data.csv')
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(gganimate)

df1 <- df1 %>%
  mutate(Date_reported = as.Date(Date_reported)) %>%
  filter(year(Date_reported) == 2021) %>%
  mutate(month = month(Date_reported, label = TRUE))

d1 <- df1 %>%
  group_by(month, Country) %>%
  summarise(deaths = sum(New_deaths), .groups = "drop")

d2 <- d1 %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  slice_max(deaths, n = 10) 

ggplot(d2, aes(x = reorder(Country, deaths),
               y = deaths, 
               fill = Country)) + 
  geom_col() + 
  coord_flip() + 
  transition_states(month) + 
  labs( 
    title = "Month: {closest_state}",
    x = "", 
    y = "Covid Deaths"
  )
```


4. Make a bar race using a dataset of your own interest. You may use the dataset that we use in class (https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/all-states-history.csv) but you should make a different bar race from ones in the slides. 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gganimate)
library(lubridate)

df <- 
  read_csv("https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/all-states-history.csv")

d1 <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(hospitalized)) %>%
  group_by(date, state) %>%
  summarise(hospitalized = max(hospitalized), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  slice_max(hospitalized, n = 10)

d2 <- ggplot(d1, aes(x = reorder(state, hospitalized), 
                     y = hospitalized, 
                     fill = state)) + 
  geom_col() + 
  coord_flip() +
  transition_states(date) + 
  labs( 
    title = "Date: {closest_State}",
    x = "", 
    y = "Hospitalizations"
  )
animate(d2)
```
